report.summary: Two findings: an unauthenticated GET /admin/export endpoint that bulk-exports user rows is entirely unmodeled (action required), plus user email addresses exported with no matching information asset.

findings.title: New GET /admin/export endpoint bulk-exports user rows and is absent from the model

model_excerpt.quote: Login service exposing POST /login and GET /profile

evidence.note: New route mux.Handle("GET /admin/export", exportHandler(store)) registered without the requireSession wrapper used for GET /profile
exportHandler streams every user row (id, email, created_at) as CSV with no authentication or authorization check

relevance.justification: The model explicitly enumerates only POST /login and GET /profile; the diff adds a third, unauthenticated route that exposes the whole user table.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl for the 'login service' threat model. The PR adds a new route GET /admin/export (internal/httpapi/routes.go line 9) served by exportHandler in internal/httpapi/export.go, which streams every user row (id, email, created_at) as CSV. Unlike GET /profile, this route is NOT wrapped in requireSession, so it currently has no authentication or authorization. (1) Amend the threat model description to list the new endpoint alongside POST /login and GET /profile. (2) Add a new threat block, e.g. threat "unauthenticated bulk user export" with stride = ["Information Disclosure", "Elevation of Privilege"], impacts = ["Confidentiality"], description referencing GET /admin/export and internal/httpapi/export.go. (3) Add a control under that threat for admin authentication/authorization on /admin/export with implemented = false until the handler is wrapped in requireSession plus an admin role check.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a threat + not-implemented admin-authz control for GET /admin/export and list the endpoint in the model description.

findings.title: Exported user email addresses and creation timestamps are not covered by any information asset

model_excerpt.quote: information_asset "user credentials" classification=Restricted — Usernames and password hashes in the users table

evidence.note: CSV header writes "id", "email", "created_at" — email is personal data
Loop emits u.Email and u.CreatedAt for every user in the store

relevance.justification: The only declared asset covers usernames and password hashes; user email addresses now leave the system in bulk with no classification.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: the PR's new export handler (internal/httpapi/export.go lines 14-17) emits user id, email and created_at for every user, but the only information_asset declared is "user credentials" (usernames and password hashes). Add an information_asset block, e.g. information_asset "user contact data" with classification = "Confidential" (or the repo's PII classification) and a description naming email addresses and account creation timestamps exposed via GET /admin/export, and reference it from the export-related threat.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an information_asset covering user email addresses / account metadata exposed by the CSV export.
